question_text: Tell me about a film or story that you like.

evaluation_guide.expected_content: A short personal description of a film or story that the student likes.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Names a film or story; gives one or two simple details about it; may say why they like it; uses some multi-syllable words so word stress can be heard.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any short answer about a film, cartoon, tale, comic, book story, or school story that the student likes is acceptable. The student does not need special knowledge or technical vocabulary.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Naming only a title with no detail; talking only about watching films in general without mentioning a specific film or story; talking about an unrelated hobby.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Listen for stress in words such as 'popular,' 'cartoon,' 'adventure,' 'interesting,' 'character,' and other multi-syllable words the student uses. Focus on whether the main stressed syllable is usually clear and correctly placed.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Mis-stressing common content words; using only one-syllable words; pausing too much so stress is unclear; giving a long retelling that becomes hard to follow; going off topic.

suggested_ideas: what kind of film or story it is
